name: Parc Monceau: the gate on the Avenue Vélasquez
note: batch1/parks.ts: Davioud's black and gilded iron, standing open. At the end of OSM's Allée de la Comtesse de Ségur; −z to the avenue.

name: Parc Monceau: the gate on the Avenue Ruysdaël
note: batch1/parks.ts: at the head of the avenue, where the Avenue Ferdousi leaves the park.

name: Parc Monceau: the gate on the Avenue Van Dyck
note: batch1/parks.ts: the Allée de la Comtesse de Ségur's west end.

name: Parc Monceau: the gate by the Rotonde
note: batch1/parks.ts: on the Boulevard de Courcelles, beside the Rotonde de Chartres.

name: Parc Monceau: the pyramid
note: batch1/parks.ts: OSM's way/757659087, historic=tomb, drawn as a box till now.

name: Parc Monceau: the Renaissance arcade
note: batch1/parks.ts: one bay of the old Hôtel de Ville. Placed from memory beside OSM's pool way/68335803: street view to confirm.

name: Parc Monceau: the bridge
note: batch1/parks.ts: on the Petite Rivière where OSM's path meets it. Its place and look from memory: street view to confirm.

name: Buttes-Chaumont: the Grotte
note: batch1/parks.ts: the rock face and mouth of the artificial cave (OSM way/125420680) and the fall inside it; the terrain has the cliff round it.

name: Parc Montsouris: the cascade
note: batch1/parks.ts: at OSM node/9176469533, rock and a thin fall.

name: Parc Montsouris: the Mire du Sud
note: batch1/parks.ts: OSM's node/3588040118, Mire de l'Observatoire.

name: Parc André-Citroën: the Ballon de Paris
note: batch1/parks.ts: on its pad in IGN's photograph, moored; it spends its days aloft.

name: Parc André-Citroën: the fountain
note: batch1/parks.ts: the grid of jets across the tilted square between the greenhouses.

name: Parc de Bercy: the wine lanes' rails
note: batch1/parks.ts: rails let into OSM's cobbled lanes, x east, z north about this point. Its `size` is small on purpose: the overhead line's poles keep clear of a standalone's radius.

name: Parc Georges-Brassens: the belfry
note: batch1/parks.ts: OSM's tower way/1035080632 and hall way/53724046, the horse market's auction hall.

name: Parc Georges-Brassens: the bull on the east
note: batch1/parks.ts: Cain's bronze, a stand-in for Tripo. OSM way/80146212.

name: Parc Georges-Brassens: the bull on the west
note: batch1/parks.ts: Cain's bronze, a stand-in for Tripo. OSM way/80146226.

name: Jardin des Plantes: the Gloriette de Buffon
note: batch1/parks.ts: Verniquet, 1788, at the top of the Labyrinthe. OSM way/1039573855.

name: Parc de la Villette: the Dragon
note: batch1/parks.ts: Hanss's steel slide in OSM's Jardin du Dragon way/81704884, from memory: street view to confirm which way it faces.

name: Jardin du Ranelagh: the bandstand
note: batch1/parks.ts: OSM way/158177310.

name: Jardin du Ranelagh: the carousel
note: batch1/parks.ts: the hand-cranked carousel, its place inside OSM's playground from memory: street view to confirm.

name: Lariboisière: the pavilions
note: Gauthier's hospital (1846–54): six stone pavilions a side on the cour d'honneur, slate roofs (aerial 48.8825 2.3535). OSM's flat tan massing, in the classical dress. The gallery is `lariboisiereGallery`.

name: Lariboisière: the court's gallery
note: batch1/hospitals.ts: the arcade round the cour d'honneur (aerial, 48.8825 2.3535), which links the pavilions. A wall of arches on three sides, a terrace on it; standing on the ground between OSM's pavilions, so not claiming them.

name: Hôpital Necker: the Carré Necker
note: Necker's 2010s block on the Rue de Sèvres side: pale cladding and long glass, not OSM's flat tan.

name: Hôpital Necker: the Pôle Mère-Enfants Laennec
note: Béatrice Ghibaudo's Laennec building (2013): pale cladding and glass, its colour by floor; the accent is from memory.

name: Hôpital Necker: Imagine
note: Jean Nouvel's Institut Imagine (2014): a glass block, tinted, on the Boulevard du Montparnasse.

name: Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou
note: Zublena's hospital (2000): white stone and glass bars round courts, its glass roofs are `hegpGlass`. Read off the aerial 48.8390 2.2735; the massing is OSM's relation/1824605.

name: Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou: the glass roofs and rotunda
note: batch1/hospitals.ts: the teal vaults over its halls and the round entrance drum on the Rue Leblanc corner, x east, z north about this point, read off IGN's aerial. Stands on OSM's massing, claims nothing. Its `size` is small on purpose: the T3's poles keep clear of a standalone's radius.

name: Hôpital Cochin: the Abbaye de Port-Royal
note: The abbey (1625), now the Port-Royal maternity's old wing: a low stone cloister under a steep slate roof.

name: Hôpital Cochin: Cornil-Brissaud
note: Cochin's brick and stone pavilions.

name: Hôpital Cochin: Maison de Solenn
note: Le Corre and Pei's Maison de Solenn (2004): a wooden lattice over its white walls; from memory.

name: École normale supérieure: the Rue d'Ulm
note: Guillaume's building (1847) round the Cour aux Ernests: stone and slate. The court's pool is `ensErnests`, its gravel in tools/gardens/paris-parks.ts.

name: École normale supérieure: the Cour aux Ernests
note: batch1/hospitals.ts: the round pool whose goldfish are all named Ernest; the aerial's pale ring at 24,−10 of the 48.8420 2.3445 grid.

name: Jussieu: the Gril
note: Albert's Grid (1958–72): dark steel and glass bars round square courts. OSM's massing in a curtain wall (the real one stands on pilotis, which a restyle can't say). The Tour Zamansky is `tourZamansky`.

name: Musée Marmottan Monet
note: The Duc de Valmy's hunting lodge (1880s) off the Ranelagh, now the Monets: a stone hôtel particulier in slate, OSM's main way.

name: Hôpital Fernand-Widal
note: The old Maison municipale de santé (Théodore Labrouste's Maison Dubois, 1858): stone wings round a court. From the candidates list when Batch 1's good ones fell away; OSM's massing, the date from memory: street view to confirm.

name: Hôpital Bretonneau
note: Belouet's children's hospital of 1901 (restored 2001), brick and stone with ceramic bands: the candidates list, massing OSM's. Street view to confirm which wings are the old ones.

name: Institut Mutualiste Montsouris
note: A modern hospital of pale panels and long glass on the Boulevard Jourdan: the candidates list, OSM's massing.

name: Fondation Cartier
note: batch1/cartier.ts: Nouvel's glass building (1994) off the Boulevard Raspail, with its free-standing screen along the boulevard. All read off IGN's aerial: OSM's way 79616736, 26 × 42 m and 32.6 m tall; the screen at 37,16 to 46,−22 of the 48.8375 2.3310 grid.
